subject: Clarify notification SLAs, evidence access delegation, and cross-border transfer steps
messages:

To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finserv-example.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Incident: potential data exposure — immediate notify & evidence access questions

Diego,

We detected anomalous activity in our tenant from late last night; our security team is still triaging. Before we get into forensics, we need to confirm two things with Redwood:

1) Your notification SLA for incidents affecting customer data (time to initial notice, followed by substantive update cadence).
2) How Redwood will provide access to forensic artifacts and whether we can request export of logs/evidence to our jurisdiction (we are limited by cross-border rules).

If you can point me to the existing clause or provide a short matrix (who notifies whom, by when, and what evidence is available), that would help our board-level reporting.

Also copied procurement as they may request an amendment if additional obligations are needed.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Security Operations
FinServe Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finserv-example.com>, procurement@finserv-example.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 19:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Incident: potential data exposure — immediate notify & evidence access questions

Diego — quick update and proposed reply below.

Our standard DPA notification language: initial notice within 24 hours of Redwood confirming we have a security event that impacts customer data; substantive update within 72 hours and then daily until resolution for severe incidents. We can provide a signed incident notice and a runbook-based evidence handoff.

Proposed short matrix (to send to FinServe):
- Initial acknowledgement: within 4 hours of receiving notice from customer/alert or within 4 hours of Redwood detection if customer is impacted.
- Formal notice (what happened & scope): within 24 hours.
- Evidence export availability: preliminary artifacts (sanitized logs) within 48 hours; full forensic export subject to legal review and subprocessor coordination — target 7 days.
- Access method: secure S3 export link (preferred) or direct transfer to customer-controlled bucket; for EU data, we can stage data in an EU region and/or provide on-prem export via secure courier if required.

Notes/risks:
- Subprocessors: our logging vendor (LogStreamCo) stores rotated logs in GCP-US by default; we have a contract with LogStreamCo that allows evidence exports but if export crosses borders we need a legal review + copy of the FinServe lawful basis.
- Escrow/forensics: we can produce MD5-verified zip bundles. For very sensitive exposures, we require an amendment for privileged transfer and audit access.

I suggest we send the matrix with a clear "next steps": request customer confirmation of desired transfer path and whether they will execute the DPA amendment for expedited cross-border export.

Reply draft (short):
Liam — thanks for flagging. We can provide an initial notice within 4 hours and a formal scope update within 24 hours. Preliminary sanitized artifacts in 48 hours; full export target 7 days pending legal/subprocessor coordination. Can you confirm whether FinServe requires the export to remain in the EU? If so, please confirm lawful basis and preferred transfer mechanism (FinServe bucket or staged Redwood EU bucket). I've attached our notify matrix draft.

Will send as soon as Ben/Karthik confirm the subproc and infra details.

Marissa
Sr. Manager, Customer Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-notify-matrix-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finserv-example.com>, procurement@finserv-example.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Incident: potential data exposure — immediate notify & evidence access questions

Quick legal note for the thread — copying counsel if needed (Megan Liu listed by procurement as external counsel).

1) Subprocessor exposure: LogStreamCo is a subprocessor for logs. Their TOU allows us to request export, but cross-border exports require us to ensure appropriate safeguards (SCCs or other transfer mechanism).
2) Evidence scope: we can produce logs, request traces, and token metadata. We cannot produce customer PII beyond what the DPA allows without a lawful basis or court order.
3) Contract amendment: if FinServe requires guaranteed exportability to a specific jurisdiction within 7 days, we should propose a narrow amendment (export SLA + liability carveouts + indemnity in case of mandated cross-border transfer).

Suggested language to include in our customer-facing note: "Preliminary artifacts will be delivered in a sanitized form. Full forensic exports that contain low-level identifiers may require additional legal approvals or an executed amendment."

If procurement wants to move fast, we can prepare a 1-page amendment and route via DocuSign — tagging SEC for review (JIRA: SEC-487).

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: amendment_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 12KB)]

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 23:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Incident: potential data exposure — immediate notify & evidence access questions

Liam — thanks for your patience. Below is Redwood's proposed short mutual action plan for notification and evidence transfer. If acceptable, we can begin the legal clearance for export and spin up the secure transfer.

Mutual Action Plan (summary):
- Initial acknowledgement: within 4 hours of FinServe's detection report (we met the ack on 15 Apr).
- Formal scope notice: within 24 hours of confirmation (Redwood sent a scope update on 16 Apr).
- Preliminary sanitized artifacts: delivered within 48 hours via secure, customer-controlled S3 link.
- Full forensic export (if requested): target 7 calendar days from request; requires customer to provide lawful-basis attestation and to execute a DPA amendment if export crosses jurisdictional controls.
- Subprocessor coordination: Redwood will engage LogStreamCo; Redwood retains responsibility to coordinate and request exports on customer's behalf.
- Evidence formats: MD5-signed zip bundles (forensic_log_export.zip), CSV logs, and a summary forensic report.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether FinServe wants the export staged in the EU (yes/no). If yes, please provide the lawful-basis attestation doc.
2) If FinServe wants a guaranteed 7-day full export SLA, reply to approve the DPA amendment and we will send the one-page amendment via DocuSign.

Links and artifacts: DocuSign for amendment: https://docusign.net/secure/participant/123456789
Drive folder (artifacts + matrix): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e
JIRA for SEC review: SEC-487

If you want to ring the on-call infra team directly I can open a SecOps bridge.

Diego Fernandez
Customer Security Lead
Redwood Inference
